steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Media representation is how media products portray people, groups, places, events, and ideas — representations are always constructed, never a simple reflection of reality.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Selection and omission: media producers choose what to include and exclude, which shapes how the subject is represented. What is left out is as important as what is included.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Stereotypes are simplified, widely recognised representations of groups — e.g. the 'dumb blonde', the 'action hero', the 'grumpy old man'. They reduce complex identities to a few traits.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Dominant representations are the most common and widely accepted portrayals in society. Alternative representations challenge or subvert these norms.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always analyse WHO is being represented, HOW they are represented, and WHY Use specific examples from CSPs — never write in general terms alone Discuss the effect of representations on audiences and society
